title: Claude AI: Why are there so many internet outages?

mock_data.title: Claude AI: Why are there so many internet outages?
mock_data.passage:
AI chatbot Claude going down is just one example of a recent IT outage. One of the main vulnerabilities of the modern internet is to blame for the growing number of incidents.

This week, AI chatbot Claude went down, leaving users unable to access the service via its maker Anthropic's website, but barely a week goes by without a similar incident at a technology giant, government website or hospital. What's causing this apparent uptick in problems?

One of the main vulnerabilities of the modern internet is the shift to cloud computing, meaning a huge range of websites and services now rely on just a handful of companies, such as Amazon and Microsoft. In the early days of the commercial internet in the 1990s, companies used to operate their own hardware and software, a bit like individual shops in a street. If one of those companies had a problem, their shop would close, but the rest would be unaffected.

These days, companies are far more likely to host all their operations on the cloud, which is like the street's road, sewer system and electrical grid rolled into one. If that goes down, then all of the shops are out of action and we all hear about it.

Sometimes, these problems can be caused by simple human error. Nothing highlights the danger of this sort of incident better than the 2024 outage when cybersecurity firm CrowdStrike released a software configuration file that took down millions of Windows computers worldwide, knocking airlines, banks, television companies and emergency-service call centres offline.

Joseph Jarnecki at the Royal United Services Institute, a UK defence think tank, says that if an outage is large and its effects wide-ranging, it is unlikely to be deliberate. Ransomware criminals, who break into systems and lock up data before demanding payment, know better than to tussle with huge technology companies full of experts – they go after smaller prey.

Tim Stevens at King's College London says that ransomware attacks are increasingly targeting small local governments and infrastructure. Their business model is to break in, lock up something that people rely on and demand a ransom, so what better to target than a town's water supply, electricity grid or local government?

In the UK, we have seen exactly that, with ransomware attacks against Hackney Council, Gloucester City Council and Leicester City Council, as well as the NHS and water suppliers. Stevens says that for as long as we have had computers, there has been a cat-and-mouse game between hackers and security experts. Unfortunately, at the moment, the hackers are ahead. "I've heard, in the last year or so, more people than normal from the profession saying that we're losing. Not just that we're behind, but we're actually losing."

State-backed hackers from countries like Russia and China are also unlikely to take down an entire cloud provider. "They definitely target them, but not to destroy and disrupt," says Jarnecki. "They're incredibly highly targeted."

An example of this would be the 2023 attack on Microsoft-run US government email accounts, which were hacked by what Microsoft said was a China-linked group. The wider service was largely unaffected, but spies got access to a treasure trove of US secrets.

Sarah Kreps at Cornell University in New York says that targeted cyberattacks are also used by nations in what is now called the grey zone – a state of tension that isn't quite peace and isn't quite war, but is a carefully considered and measured tussle that stops just short of causing all-out conflict.

"This is a form of economic sanction in a way, because so much of our GDP, our economic welfare, relies on the internet. If you can take that down, you're handicapping the adversaries' ability to generate wealth. And the ability to generate wealth is how you develop the resources to fund a war, to fund allies in a war," she says.

Kreps points out that Russia and China aren't the only ones doing this. While we occasionally hear about Western cyber warfare – GCHQ and MI6 famously hacked into computers belonging to al-Qaeda and changed a recipe for bombs into one for cupcakes – it is happening regularly, but is highly classified and done behind closed doors.

"My understanding, based on interactions with the US intelligence community, is that that is going on," says Kreps. "You do have an incentive to erode the strength of an adversary. There's a good motive behind [attacks on] Russia for their involvement in Ukraine and there's a good motive for trying to erode China's capabilities as they become a peer competitor."

Stevens says that Western countries are constrained in the scale and target of their cyberattacks because, unlike some nations, they are bound by a strong rule of law. "I have no doubt whatsoever that our intelligence agencies and our security services in general are conducting operations in cyber against Russian assets," says Stevens. "But it's hard work and there are lawyers always in the room and we are somewhat constrained. I think there's a lot of frustration about that."

On Claude, the chatbot is back up and running now, and Anthropic told New Scientist: "We've seen incredible demand for Claude over the last week and our team is doing everything we can to scale our infrastructure as quickly as possible to keep pace with the recent surge."
mock_data.passageB1:
The AI chatbot Claude had a problem and stopped working. This is just one example of internet outages that are happening more often. One of the main reasons for these problems is a weakness in how the internet works today.

This week, people could not use the AI chatbot Claude on the Anthropic website. But almost every week, a big technology company, a government website, or a hospital has a similar problem. What is causing these problems to happen more often?

One of the main weaknesses of the internet today is that many websites and services use cloud computing. This means they depend on a small number of big companies, like Amazon and Microsoft. In the past, in the 1990s, companies used to have their own computers and software. It was like having individual shops on a street. If one shop had a problem, it would close, but the other shops would still be open.

Now, companies are more likely to keep all their information and programs on the cloud. This is like the street's road, water system, and electricity all in one. If the cloud has a problem, all the “shops” on it are closed, and everyone knows about it.

Sometimes, these problems are caused by simple mistakes that people make. A good example is when the cybersecurity company CrowdStrike made a mistake in 2024. They released a software file that caused millions of Windows computers to stop working around the world. This affected airlines, banks, TV companies, and emergency call centers.

Joseph Jarnecki, from the Royal United Services Institute, says that if a problem is big and affects many people, it is probably not done on purpose. Criminals who use ransomware break into computer systems and lock up data. Then, they ask for money to unlock the data. Jarnecki says these criminals know not to fight with big technology companies that have many experts. They usually go after smaller, easier targets.

Tim Stevens from King's College London says that ransomware attacks are happening more often to small local governments and important services. The criminals break in, lock up something that people need, and ask for money. So, they might attack a town's water supply, electricity, or local government.

In the UK, this has happened with attacks on Hackney Council, Gloucester City Council, Leicester City Council, the NHS (the healthcare system), and water companies. Stevens says that hackers and security experts have been playing a game of cat and mouse since computers were invented. Now, it seems the hackers are winning. Stevens says that he has heard many people in the security business say that they are losing the fight against hackers.

Hackers who work for countries like Russia and China are also not likely to shut down an entire cloud provider. Jarnecki says that these hackers do target cloud providers, but they do not want to destroy them. They are very careful about what they attack.

For example, in 2023, hackers attacked US government email accounts that Microsoft managed. Microsoft said that the hackers were linked to China. The rest of the Microsoft service was mostly not affected, but the hackers got access to important US secrets.

Sarah Kreps from Cornell University says that countries also use cyberattacks in what is called the grey zone. This is a situation that is not quite peace and not quite war. It is a careful fight that stops before it causes a full war.

Kreps says that this is like an economic punishment. Because so much of our money and economic growth depends on the internet, if you can shut it down, you can weaken your enemy's ability to make money. And the ability to make money is how you get the resources to pay for a war or support allies in a war.

Kreps says that Russia and China are not the only countries that do this. We sometimes hear about cyber warfare from Western countries. For example, GCHQ and MI6 (British intelligence agencies) hacked into computers belonging to al-Qaeda and changed a recipe for bombs into one for cupcakes. These things happen regularly, but they are secret and done behind closed doors.

Kreps says that she understands from talking to people in the US intelligence community that these attacks are happening. She says that countries have a reason to weaken their enemies. For example, there is a good reason to attack Russia because of its involvement in Ukraine. And there is a good reason to try to weaken China's abilities as it becomes a strong competitor.

Stevens says that Western countries cannot attack as much or as easily as some other countries because they have strong laws. Stevens says that he is sure that British intelligence agencies are attacking Russian computer systems. But it is difficult, and there are always lawyers involved. He thinks that many people are frustrated by this.

The Claude chatbot is working again now. Anthropic told New Scientist that they have seen a lot of people wanting to use Claude in the last week. Their team is working hard to make their infrastructure bigger as quickly as possible to keep up with the demand.

mock_data.passageC1:
The recent disruption to the AI chatbot Claude, rendering it inaccessible to users via Anthropic's platform, serves as a stark reminder of the escalating frequency of IT outages. Indeed, hardly a week seems to pass without a similar incident befalling a major technology corporation, governmental agency, or healthcare institution. The question then arises: what accounts for this apparent surge in such disruptions?

A primary vulnerability within the modern internet infrastructure, and one that arguably underpins the growing incidence of these outages, lies in the widespread adoption of cloud computing. This paradigm shift means that a vast array of websites and online services are now critically dependent on a limited number of providers, such as Amazon and Microsoft. To illustrate, in the nascent stages of the commercial internet during the 1990s, businesses typically managed their own hardware and software, operating independently, much like individual shops on a high street. Consequently, if one entity experienced a problem, its operations would be suspended, but the remaining entities would remain unaffected.

Conversely, contemporary businesses are increasingly inclined to host their entire operational infrastructure on the cloud, which can be likened to a consolidated road, sewage, and electrical system for the entire high street. Thus, a failure in this centralized system will inevitably lead to a widespread shutdown, impacting all reliant businesses and attracting significant public attention.

In some instances, these disruptions can be attributed to simple human error. A particularly telling example is the 2024 outage triggered by cybersecurity firm CrowdStrike's release of a faulty software configuration file. This single error cascaded into a global crisis, crippling millions of Windows computers and disrupting critical services such as airlines, banks, television networks, and emergency call centres.

Joseph Jarnecki, at the Royal United Services Institute, cautions against attributing large-scale, wide-ranging outages to malicious intent. He argues that ransomware perpetrators, who infiltrate systems, encrypt data, and demand payment for its release, are unlikely to embroil themselves in direct conflict with large, well-defended technology companies. Their preferred targets are typically smaller, more vulnerable entities.

Tim Stevens at King's College London corroborates this, noting a growing trend of ransomware attacks targeting smaller local governments and infrastructure. The fundamental principle of their business model is to infiltrate and lock up essential services to extort a ransom. What could be more effective than targeting a town's water supply, electricity grid, or local government administration?

The UK has witnessed several such incidents, including ransomware attacks against Hackney Council, Gloucester City Council, Leicester City Council, the NHS, and various water suppliers. Stevens highlights the ongoing 'cat-and-mouse' game between hackers and security experts that has persisted since the advent of computers. Regrettably, he suggests that the hackers currently hold the upper hand. "I've heard, in the last year or so, more people than normal from the profession saying that we're losing. Not just that we're behind, but we're actually losing." This represents a grim assessment of the current cybersecurity landscape.

State-sponsored actors from nations like Russia and China are also unlikely to target a complete cloud provider for disruption. "They definitely target them, but not to destroy and disrupt," says Jarnecki. "They're incredibly highly targeted." Their objectives are typically more nuanced and strategic.

The 2023 attack on Microsoft-run US government email accounts, attributed by Microsoft to a China-linked group, exemplifies this approach. While the broader service remained largely unaffected, the attackers gained access to a wealth of sensitive US intelligence, highlighting the potential for espionage rather than outright disruption.

Sarah Kreps at Cornell University suggests that targeted cyberattacks are frequently employed by nations in the so-called 'grey zone' – a state of tension falling short of outright war, but involving carefully calibrated actions just shy of all-out conflict.

"This is a form of economic sanction in a way, because so much of our GDP, our economic welfare, relies on the internet. If you can take that down, you're handicapping the adversaries' ability to generate wealth. And the ability to generate wealth is how you develop the resources to fund a war, to fund allies in a war," she says. This highlights the far-reaching implications of cyber warfare.

Kreps also notes that Russia and China are not the only actors engaging in such activities. Although Western cyber warfare efforts, such as the reported GCHQ and MI6 hacking of al-Qaeda computers to alter bomb recipes, are less frequently publicized, they occur regularly, albeit under strict classification and clandestinely.

"My understanding, based on interactions with the US intelligence community, is that that is going on," says Kreps. "You do have an incentive to erode the strength of an adversary. There's a good motive behind [attacks on] Russia for their involvement in Ukraine and there's a good motive for trying to erode China's capabilities as they become a peer competitor." This underscores the strategic dimension of cyber operations.

Stevens suggests that Western nations are constrained in the scope and targets of their cyberattacks by a strong commitment to the rule of law, unlike some other countries. "I have no doubt whatsoever that our intelligence agencies and our security services in general are conducting operations in cyber against Russian assets," says Stevens. "But it's hard work and there are lawyers always in the room and we are somewhat constrained. I think there's a lot of frustration about that." This highlights the ethical considerations that shape Western cyber warfare strategies.

Regarding Claude, the chatbot has since been restored, and Anthropic stated to New Scientist: "We've seen incredible demand for Claude over the last week and our team is doing everything we can to scale our infrastructure as quickly as possible to keep pace with the recent surge." This suggests that the outage may have stemmed from an inability to meet unexpectedly high user demand, rather than a malicious attack. The underlying issue seems to be scalability.

mock_data.translation:
AI chatboti Klodning ishdan chiqishi yaqinda yuz bergan IT uzilishlarining faqat bir misolidir. Zamonaviy internetning asosiy zaifliklaridan biri hodisalar sonining o'sib borishiga sabab bo'lmoqda.

Shu hafta AI chatboti Klod ishdan chiqdi, foydalanuvchilarni o'z yaratuvchisi Anthropic veb-sayti orqali xizmatga kirish imkoniyatidan mahrum qildi, ammo texnologiya giganti, davlat veb-sayti yoki kasalxonada ham xuddi shunday hodisa yuz bermasdan deyarli bir hafta o'tmaydi. Muammolarning bu qadar ko'payishiga nima sabab bo'lmoqda?

Zamonaviy internetning asosiy zaifliklaridan biri bu bulutli hisoblashga (cloud computing) o'tishdir, ya'ni katta ko'lamdagi veb-saytlar va xizmatlar endi Amazon va Microsoft kabi bir nechta kompaniyalarga tayanadi. 1990-yillarda tijorat internetining dastlabki kunlarida kompaniyalar ko'chadagi alohida do'konlar kabi o'zlarining apparat va dasturiy ta'minotlarini boshqarardilar. Agar o'sha kompaniyalardan birida muammo yuzaga kelsa, ularning do'koni yopiladi, ammo qolganlariga ta'sir qilmaydi.

Bugungi kunda kompaniyalar o'zlarining barcha operatsiyalarini ko'chaning yo'li, kanalizatsiya tizimi va elektr tarmog'ining bir-biriga aylantirilgan bulutida (cloud) joylashtirish ehtimoli katta. Agar u ishlashdan to'xtasa, barcha do'konlar ishdan chiqadi va bu haqda hammamiz xabar topamiz.

Ba'zida bu muammolar oddiy inson xatosi tufayli yuzaga kelishi mumkin. CrowdStrike kiberxavfsizlik firmasi butun dunyo bo'ylab millionlab Windows kompyuterlarini ishdan chiqargan, aviakompaniyalar, banklar, telekompaniyalar va favqulodda vaziyatlar qo'ng'iroq markazlarini oflayn rejimga o'tkazgan dasturiy ta'minot konfiguratsiyasi faylini chiqarganida, bu kabi hodisaning xavfini 2024-yildagi uzilishdan yaxshiroq narsa tasvirlab berolmaydi.

Buyuk Britaniyaning mudofaa bo'yicha tahlil markazi – Qirollik Birlashgan Xizmatlar Institutidan Jozef Jarnetski, agar uzilish katta bo'lsa va uning oqibatlari keng miqyosli bo'lsa, buning qasddan qilingan bo'lish ehtimoli yo'q, deydi. Tizimlarni buzib kirib, to'lov potlab ma'lumotlarni qulflaydigan tovlamachi (Ransomware) jinoyatchilar mutaxasislarga boy yirik texnologiya kompaniyalari bilan o'zaro tortishmaslikni yaxshi bilishadi - ular kichikroq o'lja ortidan borishadi.

London Qirollik kollejidan Tim Stivensning aytishicha, to'lov dasturi (Ransomware) hujumlari tobora kichik mahalliy hukumatlar va infratuzilmani nishonga olmoqda. Ularning biznes modeli bostirib kirish, odamlar tayanadigan biror narsani qulflash va to'lov talab qilishdir, shuning uchun shaharning suv ta'minoti, elektr tarmog'i yoki mahalliy hukumatni nishonga olishdan ko'ra yaxshiroq nima bo'lishi mumkin?

Buyuk Britaniyada biz Xakni (Hackney) kengashi, Gloster (Gloucester) shahar kengashi va Lester (Leicester) shahar kengashiga, shuningdek NHS va suv etkazib beruvchilarga qarshi to'lov dasturi (Ransomware) hujumlari orqali xuddi shunday holat kuzatdik. Stivensning aytishicha, kompyuterlarimiz bor ekanki, xakerlar va xavfsizlik ekspertlari o'rtasida mushukqon o'yini davom etib kelmoqda. Afsuski, hozirgi vaqtda xakerlar oldinda qadam tashlashmoqda. "So‘nggi bir yilda bu sohada biz yutqazayotganimizni ta'kidlayotganlar odatdagidan ham ko‘payganini eshitmoqdamiz. Faqat orqada emas, aslida mag‘lub bo'lmoqdamiz."

Rossiya va Xitoy kabi davlatlar tomonidan qo'llab-quvvatlanuvchi xakerlar butun bir bulut (cloud) provayderini yo'q qilishi ehtimoldan yiroq emas. "Ular, albatta, ularni nishonga olishadi, lekin yo'q qilish va buzish uchun emas", deydi Jarnetski. "Ular juda yuqori darajada nishonga olingan."

Bunga misol tariqasida Microsoft tomonidan boshqariladigan AQSh hukumati elektron pochta akkauntlariga qilingan 2023-yildagi hujumni keltirish mumkin, qaysiki Microsoft "Xitoyga aloqador guruh" deb atagan hujumchilar tomonidan buzib kirilgan. Kengroq xizmat ko'rsatuvchi doira asosan zarar ko'rmadi, ammo josuslar AQShning maxfiy xazina boyliklari xazinasiga kirish imkoniyatiga ega bo'lishdi.

Nyu-Yorkdagi Kornell xalqaro universiteti professori Sara Krepsning ta'kidlashicha, maqsadli kiberhujumlar davlatlar tomonidan hozirgi kunda "kulrang hudud" - qisman tinchlik ham, urush ham bo'lmagan, lekin ehtiyotkorlik bilan o'ylangan va o'lchovli tortishuv holati deb ataladigan holda, to'liq ziddiyat keltirib chiqarmaslik uchungina ham qo'llanilmoqda.

"Bu ma'lum ma'noda iqtisodiy sanksiya shaklidir, chunki bizning yalpi ichki mahsulotimiz, iqtisodiy farovonligimiz internetga qaram. Agar siz buni to'xtata olsangiz, siz raqiblarning boylik yaratish qobiliyatini zaiflashtirasiz. Va boylik yaratish qobiliyati bu - sizning urushni moliyalash, urushdagi ittifoqchilarni moliyalash uchun resurslarni qanday rivojlantirishingizdir", deydi u.

Kreps shuni ta'kidlaydiki, buni nafaqat Rossiya va Xitoy qilyapti. Biz ba'zida G'arbiy kiber urushlari haqida eshitib turamiz - masalan, GCHQ va MI6 Al-Qoidaga tegishli kompyuterlarga kirib borib, bomba retseptlarini keks (cupcakes) ga almashtirib yuborgani - bunday amaliyotlar muntazam ravishda amalga oshirilmoqda, ammo ular chuqur maxfiylashtirilgan va pinhona olib borilmoqda.

"Mening tushunishimcha, AQSh razvedka hamjamiyati bilan o'zaro munosabatlarga asoslangan holda shuni aytishim mumkinki, bu hujumlar davom etmoqda", deydi Kreps. "Dushman kuchini yemirish uchun sizda etarli rag'bat mavjud. Ukraynadagi ishtiroki uchun Rossiyaga nisbatan (hujumlarda) va xuddi shunga o'xshab raqobatchiga aylanayotgan Xitoyning imkoniyatlarini yo'q qilishga harakat qilish uchun kuchli motiv (asos) bor."

Stivensning ta'kidlashicha, G'arb davlatlari kiberhujumlarning ko'lami va maqsadi jihatidan cheklangan, chunki ba'zi davlatlardan farqli o'laroq, ular kuchli huquq ustuvorligi qoidalari bilan bog'langan. "Menimcha, bizning razvedka agentliklarimiz va umuman xavfsizlik xizmatlarimiz Rossiya aktivlariga qarshi kibermuhitida amaliyot o'tkazmoqda", deydi Stivens. "Ammo bu og'ir ish, zudlik bilan advokatlar xonada paydo bo'ladi va biz biroz siqilib qolamiz. O'ylaymanki, bu ko'p umidsizliklarni keltirib chiqarmoqda."

Kyud bilan bog'liq vaziyatga kelsak, chatbot yana ishlamoqda va Antropik "New Scientist" ga shunday dedi: "So'nggi haftada biz Kaludga juda katta talabni ko'rdik va bizning jamoamiz so'nggi paytlardagi yuksalish(o'sish) hamnafas bo'lish uchun infratuzilmamizni iloji boricha tezroq kengaytirish uchun hamma narsani qilmoqda."

mock_data.translationB1:
Claude sun'iy intellekt chatbotida muammo yuzaga kelib, ishlamay qoldi. Bu tez-tez sodir bo'layotgan internetdagi uzilishlarning birgina misoli xolos. Ushbu muammolarning asosiy sabablaridan biri internetning bugungi kundagi ishlashidagi zaiflikdir.

Bu hafta odamlar Anthropic veb-saytida Claude sun'iy intellekt chatbotidan foydalana olmadilar. Ammo deyarli har hafta yirik texnologiya kompaniyasi, hukumat veb-sayti yoki kasalxonada shunga o'xshash muammo yuzaga keladi. Bu muammolarning tez-tez sodir bo'lishiga nima sabab bo'lmoqda?

Internetning bugungi kundagi asosiy zaifliklaridan biri shundaki, ko'plab veb-saytlar va xizmatlar bulutli hisoblashdan foydalanadi. Bu ularning Amazon va Microsoft kabi bir nechta yirik kompaniyalarga bog'liqligini anglatadi. Ilgari, 1990-yillarda kompaniyalar o'zlarining kompyuterlari va dasturiy ta'minotiga ega bo'lishardi. Bu ko'chada alohida do'konlarga ega bo'lishga o'xshardi. Agar bitta do'konda muammo bo'lsa, u yopilardi, lekin boshqa do'konlar ochiq qolardi.

Endi kompaniyalar o'zlarining barcha ma'lumotlari va dasturlarini bulutda saqlashga ko'proq moyil. Bu ko'chaning yo'li, suv tizimi va elektr ta'minoti barchasi bir joyda bo'lishiga o'xshaydi. Agar bulutda muammo bo'lsa, undagi barcha "do'konlar" yopiladi va bu haqda hamma biladi.

Ba'zan, bu muammolar odamlarning oddiy xatolaridan kelib chiqadi. Bunga yaxshi misol, 2024-yilda kiberxavfsizlik kompaniyasi CrowdStrike xato qilganida. Ular millionlab Windows kompyuterlarining butun dunyo bo'ylab ishlashini sabab bo'lgan dasturiy ta'minot faylini chiqardilar. Bu aviakompaniyalar, banklar, telekompaniyalar va favqulodda chaqiruv markazlariga ta'sir qildi.

Qirollik Birlashgan Xizmatlar Instituti xodimi Jozef Jarnecki, agar muammo katta bo'lsa va ko'p odamlarga ta'sir qilsa, u qasddan qilinmagan bo'lishi mumkinligini aytadi. Jinoyatchilar, to'lov dasturidan foydalanib, kompyuter tizimlariga kirib, ma'lumotlarni qulflab qo'yishadi. Keyin ular ma'lumotlarni ochish uchun pul so'rashadi. Jarnecki bu jinoyatchilar ko'p mutaxassislarga ega bo'lgan yirik texnologiya kompaniyalari bilan kurashmaslikni bilishlarini aytadi. Ular odatda kichikroq, osonroq nishonlarni ko'zlashadi.

King's College London xodimi Tim Stivensning aytishicha, kichik mahalliy hukumatlar va muhim xizmatlarga to'lov dasturi hujumlari tez-tez sodir bo'lmoqda. Jinoyatchilar kirib, odamlarga kerak bo'lgan narsani qulflab qo'yishadi va pul so'rashadi. Shunday qilib, ular shaharning suv ta'minoti, elektr ta'minoti yoki mahalliy hukumatiga hujum qilishlari mumkin.

Buyuk Britaniyada bu Hackney Kengashi, Gloster shahar kengashi, Lester shahar kengashi, NHS (sog'liqni saqlash tizimi) va suv kompaniyalariga hujumlar bilan sodir bo'ldi. Stivensning aytishicha, xakerlar va xavfsizlik bo'yicha mutaxassislar kompyuterlar ixtiro qilinganidan beri mushuk va sichqon o'yinini o'ynashmoqda. Endi esa, xakerlar g'alaba qozonayotganga o'xshaydi. Stivens xavfsizlik biznesidagi ko'p odamlarning xakerlarga qarshi kurashda mag'lub bo'layotganliklarini aytganini eshitganini aytadi.

Rossiya va Xitoy kabi mamlakatlar uchun ishlaydigan xakerlar ham butun bulut provayderini o'chirib qo'yish ehtimoli kam. Jarneckining aytishicha, bu xakerlar bulut provayderlarini nishonga olishadi, lekin ularni yo'q qilishni xohlashmaydi. Ular nimaga hujum qilishayotganiga juda ehtiyot bo'lishadi.

Masalan, 2023-yilda xakerlar Microsoft boshqargan AQSh hukumatining elektron pochta hisoblariga hujum qilishdi. Microsoftning aytishicha, xakerlar Xitoy bilan aloqador bo'lgan. Microsoft xizmatining qolgan qismi asosan ta'sir qilmadi, lekin xakerlar AQShning muhim sirlariga kirishga muvaffaq bo'lishdi.

Kornell universitetidan Sara Krepsning aytishicha, davlatlar kiberhujumlardan kulrang zona deb ataladigan narsada ham foydalanadilar. Bu tinchlik ham emas, urush ham emas vaziyat. Bu to'liq urushga olib kelmasdan to'xtaydigan ehtiyotkorona kurash.

Krepsning aytishicha, bu iqtisodiy jazoga o'xshaydi. Chunki bizning pulimiz va iqtisodiy o'sishimizning katta qismi internetga bog'liq, agar siz uni o'chirib qo'ysangiz, dushmaningizning pul ishlash qobiliyatini zaiflashtirishingiz mumkin. Pul ishlash qobiliyati esa urush uchun pul to'lash yoki urushda ittifoqchilarni qo'llab-quvvatlash uchun resurslarni olish usulidir.

Krepsning aytishicha, Rossiya va Xitoy buni qilayotgan yagona davlatlar emas. Biz ba'zan G'arb davlatlarining kiber urushi haqida ham eshitamiz. Masalan, GCHQ va MI6 (Britaniya razvedka agentliklari) al-Qoidaga tegishli kompyuterlarni buzib kirib, bomba uchun retseptni keks uchun retseptga o'zgartirdilar. Bu narsalar muntazam ravishda sodir bo'ladi, lekin ular sirli va yopiq eshiklar ortida amalga oshiriladi.

Krepsning aytishicha, u AQSh razvedka hamjamiyatidagi odamlar bilan gaplashib, bu hujumlar sodir bo'layotganini tushunadi. Uning aytishicha, davlatlarning dushmanlarini zaiflashtirish uchun sababi bor. Masalan, Rossiyaga Ukrainadagi ishtiroki tufayli hujum qilish uchun yaxshi sabab bor. Xitoyning kuchli raqobatchiga aylanayotganligi sababli uning qobiliyatlarini zaiflashtirishga urinish uchun ham yaxshi sabab bor.

Stivensning aytishicha, G'arb davlatlari ba'zi boshqa davlatlar kabi ko'p yoki oson hujum qila olmaydi, chunki ularda kuchli qonunlar bor. Stivensning aytishicha, u Britaniya razvedka agentliklari Rossiya kompyuter tizimlariga hujum qilayotganiga amin. Ammo bu qiyin va har doim advokatlar aralashadi. Uning fikricha, ko'p odamlar bundan hafsalasi pir bo'ladi.

Claude chatboti hozirda yana ishlamoqda. Anthropic New Scientistga o'tgan hafta Claude-dan foydalanishni xohlayotgan odamlarni ko'p ko'rganliklarini aytdi. Ularning jamoasi talabni qondirish uchun o'z infratuzilmasini imkon qadar tezroq kattalashtirish ustida qattiq ishlamoqda.

Kengroq xizmat asosan ta'sirlanmagan, ammo josuslar AQShning ko'plab muhim sirlariga kirish imkoniyatiga ega bo'lishdi.

"Bu bir jihatdan iqtisodiy sanksiya, chunki bizning YaIMning, iqtisodiy farovonligimizning katta qismi internetga bog'liq. Claude haqida aytadigan bo'lsak, chatbot yana ishlamoqda va Anthropic New Scientistga shunday dedi: "So'nggi hafta ichida Claude'ga bo'lgan talab juda katta bo'ldi va bizning jamoamiz yaqinda foydalanish o'sishiga moslashish uchun infratuzilmamizni tezda kengaytirish uchun qo'limizdan kelganini qilmoqda."
